Monte Carlo uncertainty of a bootstrap goodness-of-fit p-value

pb_gof_mc_error.Rd

Quantifies simulation uncertainty in a parametric-bootstrap goodness-of-fit tail probability.

Usage

pb_gof_mc_error(test, level = 0.95)

Arguments

test

A pb_gof object returned by pb_gof.

level

Confidence level for the exact binomial limits.

Details

The original add-one corrected p-value is \((1+k)/(1+B)\), with \(k\) selected-tail exceedances among \(B\) successful refits. The plug-in Monte Carlo standard error and exact Clopper-Pearson interval apply to the raw tail probability \(k/B\), not the add-one adjusted p-value. When no simulated value is as extreme as the observation, the plug-in standard error is zero, while the exact confidence interval has a positive upper endpoint. These calculations condition on the fitted model and successful, independent refits and do not account for selective refit failure or model misspecification.

Value

A one-row data frame with tail, p_value, tail_probability, mc_standard_error, lower, upper, exceedances, valid_replicates, and failed_replicates.

See also

pb_plot_gof, pb_lrt_mc_error

Examples

fit <- glm(vs ~ mpg, data = mtcars, family = binomial())
check <- pb_gof(fit, n = 30, seed = 1)
#> Warning: 1 of 30 bootstrap refits produced warnings (for example convergence problems).
pb_gof_mc_error(check)
#>      tail  p_value tail_probability mc_standard_error     lower     upper
#> 1 greater 0.483871        0.4666667        0.09108401 0.2834181 0.6567448
#>   exceedances valid_replicates failed_replicates
#> 1          14               30                 0
